title: NyaDrop_Incident_Response_Scenario_71c
description: Investigate and respond to a Linux/NyaDrop backdoor malware incident.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content:
The target network has been compromised by the Linux/NyaDrop backdoor malware. This malware targets MIPS-based IoT devices and opens an internet socket to remotely connect to a remote host for receiving data of any Linux executable stream intended to infect the compromised machine. The received data is saved as 'nya' ELF malware file and then executed by Linux/NyaDrop with its permission privilege on the targeted MIPS CPU architecture device. The 'nya' dropped file is deleted every time the next new attacks are successfully logged in to the MIPS machine and then updating the previously saved 'nya' malware.

The malware uses systemd services and timers for persistence and executes a malicious file named 'nya'.

Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident. You will need to identify suspicious services, determine persistence mechanisms, and identify associated malicious files. The flags you need to find are text strings.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the target host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: target
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

From the target host, you can SSH to the next-target host using the same credentials.
levels.local_content: Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Services
levels.content:
Investigate the target host for any suspicious services or processes.

Question: What is the name of the suspicious service running on the target host? The flag is a text string.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Systemd services can be checked to identify any suspicious or unfamiliar services running on the system.

hints.title: Command Hint
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all running services.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for services that are unfamiliar or do not belong to standard system services.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

Question: What is the persistence mechanism used by the suspicious service? The flag is a text string.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Persistence mechanisms can often be found in systemd timers that trigger services periodically.

hints.title: Command Hint
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all systemd timers.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for timers that are associated with the suspicious service identified in the previous step.

levels.title: Identify Associated File
levels.content:
Identify the file associated with the suspicious activity.

Question: What is the name of the file associated with the suspicious service? The flag is a text string.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Malicious files are often found in the home directory of the user running the suspicious service.

hints.title: Command Hint
hints.content: Use the command `ls -la /home/cyrano` to list files in the user's home directory.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for files with unusual names or permissions that might indicate malicious activity.
